name: Squall Requiem

civilization.name: The Vethara Ascendancy
civilization.notes: The Vethara were a spacefaring civilization that achieved interplanetary colonization before a self-replicating weapons system turned against its creators. The grey-goo scenario consumed all organic matter on the surface within decades. The nanite swarm eventually exhausted its fuel supply and went dormant, leaving behind a world of perfectly preserved infrastructure and no living inhabitants.

geological_features: Artificially leveled plains where cities once stood
Deep bore-shafts leading to collapsed underground transit networks
Coastlines of empty ocean basins, the water consumed during the nanite event
specific_features: Intact but lifeless cities with functioning power grids running on geothermal taps
A dormant nanite layer in the topsoil that activates unpredictably when disturbed
Orbital debris ring from destroyed Vethara space stations
resources: Vethara computational hardware of extraordinary sophistication
Geothermal power infrastructure still generating energy
Refined construction materials in abandoned cities
description: Squall Requiem is a world that should be alive but is not. Its cities stand intact beneath a thin, hazy sky, their towers and plazas and transit lines preserved with a completeness that suggests the inhabitants simply vanished between one heartbeat and the next. The oceans are gone, leaving vast basins of cracked grey sediment. The atmosphere has thinned to a whisper as the biosphere that once replenished it has been entirely erased, and the wind that moves through the empty streets carries nothing but fine, sterile dust.

The wrongness of Squall Requiem is felt before it is understood. Buildings stand with their doors open, vehicles rest in orderly rows, and public screens still cycle through information feeds in a language no living being speaks. Power flows through the grid from geothermal plants that will run for centuries yet, illuminating streetlights for no one and heating habitation units whose occupants were dissolved at the molecular level. It is a world frozen in the moment of its death, and the silence is absolute.

The Vethara Ascendancy reached for the stars and grasped them briefly before hubris consumed them. Their self-replicating defense system, designed to neutralize biological threats, suffered a catastrophic targeting error and classified all organic matter as hostile. The nanites consumed everything, from the Vethara themselves down to the last bacterium in the soil, before their fuel reserves depleted and they entered dormancy. Xenoarchaeologists have pieced together the timeline from data archives still running in the capital, and the records make for harrowing reading: the entire extinction took less than three standard years.

The treasures of Squall Requiem are immense and the dangers commensurate. Vethara technology was decades ahead of current standards, and a single intact computational core could revolutionize processing across multiple sectors. But the dormant nanites remain in the soil, and disturbances of sufficient magnitude have been shown to trigger localized reactivation events. Every expedition operates under strict protocols, and the graveyard of failed salvage ships in orbit serves as a reminder that the weapon that killed the Vethara has not yet fully died.
